headline: Thomson Reuters told courts across a dozen states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario that intruders took C-Track case files holding sealed proceedings and Social Security numbers, while attackers hijacked Coder's registry to ship credential-stealing Terraform modules and turned a critical Elementor Pro flaw into webshells on WordPress servers.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep going after the plumbing that delivers trusted code, hijacking Coder's Cloudflare infrastructure to serve credential-stealing Terraform modules days after a Border Gateway Protocol hijack poisoned Softaculous update servers.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Coder Registry Hijack Delivers Malicious Terraform Modules

emerging_trends.text: Unit 42 watched operators lean on commercial AI tools to sort and exfiltrate stolen data from Latin American organizations, and researchers clocked frontier agents compressing a two-week breach into 10 hours, shrinking the window defenders get to react.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Attackers Wield AI Against Latin American Targets

emerging_trends.text: Security software itself keeps turning into the way in, with a public proof-of-concept escalating privileges through the macro remediation routine in the CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor while publicly disclosed S/MIME defects sit unpatched in Cisco Secure Email.

topics.title: FalconFlank Zero-Day Hits CrowdStrike Falcon
topics.latest_developments: The researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse, also called Nightmare Eclipse, published a proof-of-concept for FalconFlank, a privilege-escalation zero-day that abuses the malicious-macro remediation routine in the CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor, the same researcher whose HardBreacher exploit forced a Kaspersky patch on August 31, 2026; Cisco patched CVE-2026-20212, a CVSS 9.8 bug in 10 Silicon One-based Nexus 9000 switches that gives an unauthenticated remote attacker root code execution, shipped an IOS XR hardening release bundling seven CVEs with no workaround for any version, and left publicly disclosed S/MIME flaws in Secure Email unpatched; Hewlett Packard Enterprise patched a critical remote-code-execution flaw in its ArubaOS-CX network operating system, and Plex told users to update desktop clients and media servers immediately.
topics.summary: FalconFlank turns a defensive feature of the Falcon endpoint agent into a path from a local account to full control of the host. The unpatched Cisco Secure Email defects can expose the contents of encrypted mail; apply the Nexus, IOS XR, ArubaOS-CX, and Plex updates now and watch for a CrowdStrike sensor release.

sources.title: Researcher Releases FalconFlank PoC Showing Privilege Escalation in CrowdStrike Falcon
Cisco Warns of Unpatched Secure Email Flaws, Patches Critical Switch Vulnerabilities
Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Remote Attackers Run Code as Root
HPE patches critical ArubaOS-CX remote code execution flaw

topics.title: Microsoft Details Spring Ring Teams Impersonation, Node.js Abused as Loader
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published its own technical writeup of a human-operated intrusion campaign, matching the Spring Ring operation Unit 42 first disclosed, that abuses Microsoft Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT support and deploy a Node.js-based implant for lateral movement, while Symantec separately documented a distinct campaign running since February 2026 that abuses the trusted node.exe runtime to deliver payloads against government departments, technology companies, and hotels; Microsoft also reported that phishing crews now hide invisible Unicode characters inside words so email filters misread them, a trick called ASCII smuggling that crossed over from AI prompt-injection research, and Dark Reading detailed Phantom Deal, a campaign that studies large enterprises in detail and dupes midlevel employees into wiring large sums against fabricated merger and acquisition paperwork.
topics.summary: Both intrusion campaigns exploit the fact that node.exe carries Microsoft's own code-signing trust, letting malicious JavaScript payloads slip past defenses tuned to flag unfamiliar executables. Organizations should restrict external Teams collaboration requests, treat unexpected node.exe network activity as suspicious, and require voice confirmation on wire transfers tied to deal paperwork.

sources.title: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
Threat Gang 'Springs' Vishing Attacks on Microsoft Teams Users
Attackers Turn Trusted Node.js Runtime Into Malware Delivery Tool in Targeted Attacks
ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion

topics.title: Russian Malware Indictment and Pro-Ukraine Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: A federal grand jury in California indicted Searzhudin Tamirlanovich Aktulaev, 40, a Russian national who since at least June 2016 used fake accounts on a freelance employment platform to push malware to roughly 80,000 users; police in Cyprus arrested him in May 2025, he arrived in the United States under extradition in August 2026, and he appeared in San Francisco federal court on August 31, 2026, facing up to 20 years on conspiracy, transmission of malicious code, and aggravated identity theft counts. Separately, the Russian security firm F6 described VantaCore, a new pro-Ukraine group running custom ransomware against at least seven Russian companies.
topics.summary: Aktulaev's scheme baited freelancers with job files that carried the malware. Hackers also breached payment accounts behind two Russian fundraising projects supporting Ukrainians and political prisoners, exposing donor email addresses and limited card data.

sources.title: Russian man indicted for spreading malware to 80,000 freelancers
Russian national facing 20 years for malware campaign that infected 80,000 freelancers

topics.title: Thomson Reuters C-Track Breach Exposes Court Records
topics.latest_developments: Thomson Reuters said an unauthorized party took files in March 2026 from C-Track, the court case management platform its West Publishing Corporation unit sells, and that West Publishing found the activity on June 30, 2026; the exposure covers courts in 11 to 12 U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada, and a subset of the records carries names and Social Security numbers alongside sealed proceedings.
topics.summary: C-Track handles case management for courts, and the stolen data reaches sealed matters and personal information well beyond routine public dockets. Thomson Reuters posted separate notification pages for affected individuals in the United States and Canada and is contacting affected courts directly.

sources.title: Thomson Reuters reveals breach that exposed U.S. and Canadian court records
US and Canadian court data exposed in Thomson Reuters breach
Thomson Reuters Court Software Breach May Have Exposed SSNs and Sealed Data

topics.title: WordPress Plugin Flaws Draw Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Attackers began exploiting CVE-2026-32475, a recently patched critical flaw in the Elementor Pro plugin, to plant webshells and run arbitrary commands on WordPress hosts, while researchers assigned CVE-2026-19949 to the unauthenticated SQL injection in the All-in-One WP Migration and Backup plugin and put the exposed population above 3 million sites.
topics.summary: Both plugins sit on millions of WordPress installations, and either bug hands an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution on the web server. Site owners should update Elementor Pro and All-in-One WP Migration and Backup now, then hunt for unfamiliar PHP files and new administrator accounts.

sources.title: Critical Elementor Pro flaw exploited to take over WordPress sites
Over 3 Million WordPress Sites Affected by Migration Plugin Vulnerability
WordPress backup plugin flaw exposes millions of sites to takeover attacks

topics.title: Attackers Wield AI Against Latin American Targets
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 documented an ongoing campaign against organizations in Latin America in which the operators lean on commercial AI tools to sort and exfiltrate stolen data, and left operational-security errors that let defenders map and disrupt the infrastructure; Dark Reading separately reported that frontier AI agents drove one large-scale breach from start to finish in 10 hours, work that took human crews about two weeks.
topics.summary: The crew's AI usage leaves distinctive outbound traffic and artifacts that defenders can hunt. Security teams should log and inspect connections from servers and workstations to AI service endpoints, then treat unexplained ones as exfiltration.

sources.title: Attackers Expose Ongoing AI Tool Use Targeting Organizations in Latin America
AI Gives Cybercriminals a Dangerous Time Advantage
AI 'Machine Speed' Cuts 2-Week Attack Down to 10 Hours

topics.title: Coder Registry Hijack Delivers Malicious Terraform Modules
topics.latest_developments: Attackers compromised Coder's Cloudflare infrastructure and added unauthorized registry servers that handed developers Terraform modules carrying credential-stealing code, and GitGuardian separately found that a recent Shai-Hulud infostealer worm variant now sweeps 469 credential locations across developer environments, continuous integration and deployment tooling, cloud configurations, and AI tool configs, up from 189 paths in earlier versions.
topics.summary: Coder sells cloud development environments, and its registry feeds Terraform modules straight into customer infrastructure pipelines, so a poisoned module runs with build-time credentials. Engineering teams should rotate secrets that touched Coder module pulls and pin registry sources their Terraform configurations trust.

sources.title: Coder's registry infrastructure compromised to push malicious modules
Shai-Hulud's Reach Just Grew to 469 Credential Locations. Here's What That Means

topics.title: IDScan.net Tied to 153 Million License Scans
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek named IDScan.net, the Louisiana identity-verification vendor, as the likely source of the more than 153 million United States and Canadian driver's license images now for sale on a dark-web service, and an Ars Technica reporter found their own license in the trove within hours of renting a car.
topics.summary: Businesses scan customer licenses through IDScan.net at rental counters, bars, and dispensaries, and the scans include the photograph and every field on the card. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an investigation; consumers should freeze credit files and treat license-based identity checks as compromised.

sources.title: 153 Million Driver License Images Offered on Dark Web
I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale

topics.title: Pegasus Zero-Click Infects Serbian Activist
topics.latest_developments: Citizen Lab, working with Belgrade's SHARE Foundation, confirmed that an iMessage zero-click exploit planted NSO Group's Pegasus spyware on the iPhone of a member of Serbia's student protest movement, and forensic researchers now count at least 14 Serbians targeted with advanced spyware since December 2025, among them a member of Parliament, a local opposition politician, and student protesters.
topics.summary: Pegasus is commercial spyware NSO Group sells to government clients; a zero-click chain takes the phone without the owner touching anything. Serbian civil-society staff and organizers facing this threat should turn on Apple's Lockdown Mode and seek forensic review of their devices.

sources.title: Pegasus Zero-Click Spyware Exploit Infects Serbian Student Movement Member's iPhone
Large group of Serbian opposition, activist figures targeted with spyware

topics.title: Manchester Airports Group Leak Follows Ransom Refusal
topics.latest_developments: The extortion crew behind the Manchester Airports Group hack published roughly 550 gigabytes of stolen files covering 8.8 million people after the airport operator refused to pay, and the group says it got in through exposed administrator keys.
topics.summary: Manchester Airports Group runs Manchester, Stansted, and East Midlands airports, and the dumped files hold customer, booking, and travel records. Travelers who flew through those three airports should expect phishing that quotes real itinerary details.

sources.title: Manchester Airports Group Data on 8.8 Million People Leaked After Ransom Refusal

business_politics.latest_developments: Volkswagen's board approved a plan Thursday, September 3, to cut roughly 50,000 more jobs and shrink the model portfolio, doubling the reduction the carmaker had already set and leaving the future of its European assembly plants open.
business_politics.summary: Volkswagen, Europe's largest carmaker, is restructuring on a historic scale as European sales stay lackluster and Chinese manufacturers take share. The surprise decision puts tens of thousands of German industrial jobs and the utilization of the company's European plants in play.

business_politics.title: Yen Surges as Japan Rate Bets Build
business_politics.latest_developments: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said September 3 he would support holding rates steady if August inflation data cooperates, and the Dow climbed more than 600 points as Treasury yields fell, the WSJ Dollar Index dropped 0.57% to 95.15, and traders cut the odds of a rate hike to a coin flip; Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill argued the same day for a British rate rise to keep inflation from staying above target.
business_politics.summary: Japan's currency sits at the center of the global bond rout, and Japanese data released August 28 confirmed that Tokyo and Washington spent a record $98.7 billion propping up the yen last month. Waller's remarks cut against Chair Kevin Warsh's rate-hike signal from Jackson Hole, and markets now wait on Friday's August employment report.

business_politics.latest_developments: Crude futures ended September 3 little changed as traders priced in a longer conflict following this week's resumption of strikes, the European Union entered winter with its lowest gas stocks on record, and The Economist reported that Iran's axis of resistance has splintered after three years of war, with its proxies now acting on their own.
business_politics.summary: The carrier USS Abraham Lincoln's nine months at sea has become the emblem of the strain the Iran war puts on American naval and air rotations, which now run well past normal lengths. Europe's thin gas storage leaves the continent exposed to any further disruption to energy supply.

business_politics.latest_developments: Senator Thom Tillis called for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's firing as the aftershocks from Army Secretary Dan Driscoll's resignation continued to rattle Washington, the Wall Street Journal reported September 3, deepening turmoil atop the Pentagon while it wages the war against Iran.
business_politics.summary: Driscoll's resignation touched off a leadership fight inside the Defense Department that has drawn in Senate Armed Services Committee Republicans like Tillis, raising questions about Hegseth's own standing at a moment when U.S. forces remain engaged across the Middle East.

business.title: Judge Orders Allegheny County to Keep Its Pension Sound
business.latest_developments: A judge ruled Thursday, September 3, that Allegheny County must by law keep its employee pension system actuarially sound, then stopped short of ordering steps to shrink the fund's roughly $1.4 billion deficit and gave the county time to fix it.
business.summary: Allegheny County's retirement fund covers county employees and retirees and carries about $1.4 billion in unfunded liability. The ruling fixes a legal duty to close that gap and leaves the timing and the means to county government.

sources.title: Judge rules Allegheny County must keep pension fund sound, grants time to fix $1.4B deficit

business.summary: The 30-year rate tracks long-term Treasury yields, which have run up since the Iran war drove oil prices higher, and the increase raises monthly payments for Pittsburgh-area buyers already competing for a thin supply of listings.

reading.title: Are We at War with AI Agent "Civilizations"?
reading.summary: Newport returns to the July hacking attack on OpenAI after the company published more detail, and questions the framing that autonomous agent systems now constitute adversarial civilizations.

glance.text: Attackers keep hitting the code-delivery plumbing, hijacking Coder's Cloudflare infrastructure to serve credential-stealing Terraform modules while webshells land through the patched Elementor Pro flaw on WordPress hosts.

links.title: Coder Registry Hijack Delivers Malicious Terraform Modules
WordPress Plugin Flaws Draw Active Exploitation

glance.text: A public proof-of-concept for FalconFlank escalates privileges through the malicious-macro remediation routine in CrowdStrike's Falcon Sensor, making the defensive stack itself the way in.
Unit 42 tracked operators using commercial AI tools to sort and exfiltrate data stolen from Latin America, while Newport questions framing OpenAI's July breach as agent warfare.

links.title: Attackers Wield AI Against Latin American Targets
Are We at War with AI Agent "Civilizations"?

glance.text: Microsoft published its own writeup of the Spring Ring Teams impersonation campaign, as Citizen Lab confirmed a zero-click Pegasus infection on a Serbian student protester's iPhone.

links.title: Microsoft Details Spring Ring Teams Impersonation, Node.js Abused as Loader

glance.text: Volkswagen's board doubled its reduction with roughly 50,000 more job cuts, while Christopher Waller's openness to holding rates steady sent the Dow up more than 600 points.

links.title: Yen Surges as Japan Rate Bets Build

glance.text: Severe thunderstorms with tornado warnings battered Western Pennsylvania as South Franklin Township's water outage reached day two, and Chris Deluzio joined calls to fire Pete Hegseth.
